History of Present Illness:
65-year-old woman. Three days of right upper abdominal pain, fever and nausea. She has no history of chronic liver disease.

Physical Examination:
Right upper-quadrant tenderness with localized guarding. Temperature 38.0 C; heart rate 88/min; BP 128/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 11.8 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 290 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 135 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 42 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 68 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 53 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 105 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen: distended stone-containing gallbladder with wall thickening and surrounding inflammation; a small adjacent fluid pocket lacks rim enhancement. No free air.
